statement.p: Parameterize the plane that contains the three points

Use s and t for the parameters in your parameterization and enter your formula as a single vector, with angle brackets, for example, \displaystyle{\langle 1 + s + t, s - t, 3 - t \rangle}. Each component should be a function of the form a+bs+ct where a,b,c are appropriate real numbers.

solution.p: Let \displaystyle{P={\left\lt -4,-2,3\right>}}, \displaystyle{Q={\left\lt -8,-6,4\right>}}, \displaystyle{R={\left\lt 5,0,35\right>}} be vectors representing the three given points.

The displacement vectors\displaystyle{\overrightarrow{PQ} = Q-P = {\left\lt -4,-4,1\right>} } and\displaystyle{\overrightarrow{PR} = R-P = {\left\lt 9,2,32\right>} } are parallel to the given plane so \displaystyle{\vec{r}(s,t) = {\left\lt -4,-2,3\right>}+s{\left\lt -4,-4,1\right>}+t{\left\lt 9,2,32\right>} = {\left\lt 9t-\left(4+4s\right),2t-\left(2+4s\right),3+s+32t\right>}} is one way to parametrize the plane. There are many other ways, of course.
